title: Binary finite support normalization in the canonical origin category
statement: Fix a finite operation stage S [def-sf-operation-stages]. Restrict inverse coefficient realization to bounded constructible objects, obtaining originInclusion into the full bounded-below etale-origin category; existence of the property is [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. For a quasi-compact f and compactification c, originSupportComparison is the explicit support realization followed by [def-sf-origin-candidate-comparison] to the canonical compactification. For two quasi-compact maps f,g and arbitrary cf,cg,cfg, applying originInclusion to the inverse S.finite.composition and then originSupportComparison for fg equals the two successive originSupportComparisons followed by the canonical originComposition [thm-sf-comp-composition]. This statement is binary, tensor-free, and makes no projection or three-map associativity assertion.

proof.text: Construct originInclusion and originSupportComparison from the fixed inverse realization and its bounded etale-origin property, exactly as before. At each constructible input, choose a bounded-below etale witness inside the proof. Regard the canonical realized etale witness as a retained RefinementFiniteLevelOrigin and use coefficient units and counits to construct the input isomorphism required by finiteCompositionNormalization.

The generic proved transport_normalization calculation cancels coefficient equivalence units and counits in the finiteCompositionNormalization field of the operation datum. It identifies the two fixed-scalar support comparisons with the candidate compositor. To identify the witnessed compositor, evaluate lem-sf-finite-support-candidate-composition at the retained etale input and use its naturality to transport across refinementFixedWitnessIso.

Apply the faithful origin inclusion to natural transformations. Its image of originSupportComparison is its fixed-scalar comparison followed by towerCandidateComparison, by the preimage construction. Use the interchange law for whiskering to move the first support comparison through the second candidate comparison. The proved supportComparison_candidate_path calculation groups the three candidate factors and cancels the final inverse comparison. Combine it with the coefficient normalization in the functor category, before evaluating any concrete derived morphism. Faithfulness returns the required equality in the origin category.

theorem originSupportComparison_composition (S : SixFunctorFiniteOperations D C E n hn)
    {X Y Z : SixFunctorSpace D} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [QuasiCompact f.hom.left] [QuasiCompact g.hom.left]
    (cf : Compactification f.hom.left) (cg : Compactification g.hom.left)
    (cfg : Compactification (f ≫ g).hom.left) :
    letI := cf.hasCompactification
    letI := cg.hasCompactification
    letI := cfg.hasCompactification
    letI : HasCompactification (f.hom.left ≫ g.hom.left) := cfg.hasCompactification
    letI : QuasiCompact (f ≫ g).hom.left :=
      inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact (f.hom.left ≫ g.hom.left))
    letI := Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n hn
    Functor.whiskerRight (S.finite.composition f g cf cg cfg).inv
        (originInclusion (C := C) (E := E) (n := n) (hn := hn) Z) ≫
      (originSupportComparison S (f ≫ g) cfg).hom =
    Functor.whiskerLeft (S.finite.support f cf) (originSupportComparison S g cg).hom ≫
      Functor.whiskerRight (originSupportComparison S f cf).hom
        (originCompactSupport
          (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n)) g.hom.left) ≫
      Functor.whiskerLeft (originInclusion (C := C) (E := E) (n := n) (hn := hn) X)
        (originComposition
          (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n))
          f.hom.left g.hom.left).hom
